item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00261","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C25","C12","C22"],"selected_candidate_label":"C25","confidence":0.94,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C25 plausibly supplied a concrete template for the child's central response to a proposed summit: affirm willingness to negotiate and meet personally, reject a meeting lacking prospects for substantive results, require advance diplomatic or ministerial exploration, and include other governments whose interests are implicated. The child closely adapts C25's distinctive formulation that a top-level meeting must offer a genuine prospect of advancing peace, while updating the factual case against Soviet conduct. C12 and C22 share related summit-preparation arguments, but C25 contains the closest combination of language and operative reasoning.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"I have many times personally pledged myself, regardless of every kind of personal consideration, to meet with anyone at anytime if there is any serious promise of productive results.","parent_excerpt":"I have repeatedly stated that there is nothing I would not do to advance the cause of a just and durable peace.","explanation":"Both establish an expansive personal willingness to meet, conditioned by the prospect of advancing peace rather than by personal considerations."},{"child_excerpt":"There is nothing in the words or actions of the government of the Soviet Union which gives me any reason to believe that the meeting you suggest would hold any such promise. I would not wish to participate in a mere gesture...","parent_excerpt":"But meetings between us do not automatically produce good results... [they] involve a danger of disillusionment, dejection and increased distrust if in fact the meetings are ill-prepared... or if they are used primarily for propaganda.","explanation":"The child reuses the parent's rationale for declining an inadequately grounded summit: a meeting is not valuable as a gesture and can be harmful without substantive prospects."},{"child_excerpt":"If Soviet representatives should wish to discuss concrete measures to reduce tensions my representatives, including the Secretary of State, are always available for this purpose. Should such exploratory discussions reveal... some prospect of fruitful results then I personally would be prepared to meet and negotiate... with the heads of other governments as their interests were involved.","parent_excerpt":"It would be essential that prior to such a meeting these complex matters should be worked on in advance through diplomatic channels and by our Foreign Ministers... so that it can be ascertained that such a top-level meeting would, in fact, hold good hope of advancing the cause of peace and justice in the world. Arrangements should also be made for the appropriate inclusion... of other governments...","explanation":"This is a strongly parallel sequence of administrative machinery: preliminary diplomatic and foreign-minister discussions, a test for likely success, then a leaders' meeting with other interested governments included."}]}
